records.note: Idols mislead many; allegiance to Abraham and mercy for dissenters. No specific earlier passage directly checked.

Abraham places descendants in an uncultivated valley beside the sacred House and asks for prayer, attraction of people, and fruit. Genesis 21:14–21 concerns Hagar and Ishmael in the wilderness of Beersheba, without a sacred House or the same prayer.

candidates.relationship: shared Abraham-family wilderness setting with major geographical and narrative differences
candidates.pending: Compare Hebrew critical edition, Septuagint and ancient witnesses; avoid equating Beersheba with Mecca; establish manuscript dating and scholarship.

records.note: God knows concealed and revealed things, on earth and in heaven; generic omniscience alone does not establish textual dependence.
Abraham praises God for Ishmael and Isaac in old age. Genesis 16:15–16 and 21:1–5 narrate births of Ishmael and Isaac respectively, but do not contain this combined praise prayer.

candidates.relationship: named-person narrative overlap with differing literary presentation
candidates.pending: Check both passages in Hebrew and Septuagint with edition and manuscript provenance; avoid treating shared names as proof of dependence.

records.note: Abraham asks that he and descendants maintain prayer and that supplication be accepted. Genesis 12:7–8 describes Abram building an altar and calling on God, not a matching descendants-prayer.
